message.content:
I'm doing a game-feel/art-direction audit of a top-down 3D LLM-NPC town game (C++ / raylib). I need a precise, evidence-backed inventory of the VISUAL layer as it exists RIGHT NOW. Report facts only with file:line evidence — no recommendations, no praise, just what is actually there.

Read these and report concretely:
- src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp and .hpp — everything drawn each frame. What primitives/models render the world (ground, roads, buildings, fountain, props, cars). How are characters drawn (composite primitives vs models)? What is the exact color palette / material tinting? Lighting model (shaders, ambient, directional)? Fog. Day/night sky/light. Nameplates/labels. Any post-processing.
- src/app/Assets.cpp and .hpp — what asset packs/models are loaded (KayKit?), which building/prop/vehicle stems exist, the size-contract (SizeSpec Fill/Uniform) system, fallbacks when assets missing.
- src/core/DayNight.hpp — the sky/light curves.
- src/core/CharacterParts.cpp/.hpp — the socket/composite character part system, categories, palettes.
- Any shader files (.glsl/.fs/.vs) or inline shader strings.

Specifically answer: (1) What reads as intentional art direction vs placeholder primitives? (2) What is the actual color/lighting mood? (3) How coherent is the mix of KayKit models + primitive composites + shader fog? (4) Is there any texture/material work or is it flat-shaded solids? Give me a concrete map with line numbers so I can cite it in an audit document.

I now have a complete picture of the visual layer. Here is the evidence-backed inventory.

---

# Visual Layer Inventory — LLM-NPC Town (C++/raylib)

## A. World rendering — what draws each frame

All world geometry is emitted in `RaylibRenderer::drawCity` (`src/app/RaylibRenderer.cpp:165-252`).

**Ground plane** — a single flat `DrawPlane` sized to the whole map, flat grass color (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:169`).

**Roads** — two code paths (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:177-205`):
- If the KayKit road models `road_straight`, `road_straight_crossing`, `road_junction` are loaded, streets are laid as tiled models on a 16-unit pitch, with junction art at the four crossings and zebra-crossing (`crossing`) tiles on the arms (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:180-199`). Tile draw = `drawRoadTile` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:63-75`), which pins thickness to `kRoadThickness = 0.05f` (line 68) and floats the slab at y=0.01 to avoid z-fighting (line 73).
- Fallback with no models: two flat asphalt `DrawCube` strips (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:201-204`).

**Block slabs** — 3×3 grid of flat `DrawCube` slabs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:208-215`): center block = pale-stone plaza (`kPlaza`), the NE block is skipped to stay grass (park), all others = `kSidewalk`.

**Buildings & props** — iterate `city.buildings()`, each keyed off collision AABBs (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:223-251`):
- Fountain special-cased by id before model lookup → composite primitives (line 227-230).
- Otherwise `modelForBuilding` returns a KayKit model, scaled by SizeSpec: `Uniform` → `drawModelUniform` (line 234), `Fill` → `drawModelFittedToAABB` (line 237). Both draw with `WHITE` tint (i.e. no tint; material/vertex colors only).
- No model → fallback `DrawCube` + `DrawCubeWires`, tinted by a hash of `facadeKind` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:242-249`).

**Fountain** — fully procedural, built from `DrawCylinder`/`DrawCylinderWires` primitives (`drawFountain`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:82-115`): stone basin, mid column + bowl, finial, plus translucent water discs. Colors are hardcoded `kStone/kStoneDark/kWater` (lines 87-89). Comment at 77-81 states the KayKit pack has no fountain model, so it is composed from primitives.

**Cars, benches, traffic lights, bushes, dumpsters, trash** — these are all KayKit models routed through the same building/prop path (curated map, see section D), sized `Uniform`.

## B. Characters — two entirely separate systems

**1. Rigged glTF pack characters** — `drawCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:254-306`). Real animated glTF models (`character->model`) with clip selection (idle/walk/gesture/death, lines 267-269), CPU skinning via `UpdateModelAnimation` (line 286), uniform-scaled to 1.8 units tall (lines 291-296), drawn `WHITE` (no tint). Fallback when no pack: a single marker `DrawCylinder`+wires (lines 259-262). Mood shown as a billboarded baked face texture above the head (`DrawBillboard`, lines 301-305).

**2. Composite primitive characters** (player-created) — `drawCompositeCharacter` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:308-382`). Pure primitives assembled from the socket system: tapered `DrawCylinder` body (line 347), `DrawSphere` head (350), sphere/cylinder hair variants (352-361), sphere/cube eyes (364-369), and a generic `DrawCube` for any part without a bespoke shape (378). Colored by flat palette (skin/hair/outfit, lines 327-329) plus a hardcoded `dark{38,38,44}` (330). Procedural walk-bob via `sin` (line 334); no skeleton (header note `RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).

These two systems coexist: NPCs/remote players use the rigged glTF path; player-created avatars use the primitive-composite path. They are visually different construction methods sharing only the 1.8-unit height contract.

**Viewmodel (first-person weapon)** — `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`): hardcoded `DrawCubeV` boxes, a table of two specs — Fist (skin cube) and Pistol (dark cube + grip cube), lines 393-396. No models.

## C. Lighting, fog, sky, post-processing

**There is no real lighting model** — no directional/ambient light, no normals-based shading. "Light" is a single scalar `lightLevel` that multiplies fragment RGB.

**Fog shader** — the only shader, defined inline as GLSL 330 string constants in `Assets.cpp`:
- Vertex: `kFogVertexShader` (`Assets.cpp:29-45`) — passes world-space position through `matModel`.
- Fragment: `kFogFragmentShader` (`Assets.cpp:47-66`). It does three things: standard `texture0 * colDiffuse * fragColor` (line 60); a **warm tint** multiply `vec3(1.06, 1.0, 0.92)` times `lightLevel` (line 61); exponential-squared distance fog `1 - exp(-d*d)` blending toward `fogColor` (lines 62-64). So day/night "lighting" is just this per-fragment brightness multiply — flat, non-directional.

Compiled via `LoadShaderFromMemory` (`Assets.cpp:78`); degrades to plain look on failure (line 95-97). Fog density hardcoded `0.006f` (`Assets.cpp:89`). The shader is assigned to every city-model material (`Assets.cpp:265-269`) and every character material (`Assets.cpp:226-230`). The renderer also wraps the whole primitive batch in `BeginShaderMode` so ground/slabs/fountain/viewmodel haze identically (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:154-160`, ended at `endFrame` 425-428).

**Day/night** — `DayNight.hpp`. Sky is four bands (night/dawn/day/dusk) with linear blends (`skyColorAt`, lines 36-49). Palette: day sky `135,190,235` (light blue), night `16,22,44` (deep navy), dusk `222,136,84` (warm orange), with warmth peaking mid-dusk (lines 25-27, 42-47). `lightLevelAt` (lines 54-65): 1.0 daylight → 0.35 night, blended across the same dawn/dusk windows. `setTimeOfDay` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:121-135`) drives sky color, `lightLevel`, and the shader's fogColor from these curves; sky and fog always share the same color. `ClearBackground(renderer.skyColor())` at `main.cpp:935`.

## Direct answers to your four questions

**(1) Intentional art direction vs placeholder primitives.**
- Reads as *intentional*: the KayKit city-bits models for buildings/roads/cars/props (curated landmark silhouettes, `Assets.cpp:108-127`), the KayKit rigged adventurers with named animation clips, the four-band day/night sky+fog color story (`DayNight.hpp:25-27`), and the warm-flat ground/asphalt/plaza palette (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:20-24`, comment "warm, low-poly-friendly flats").
- Reads as *placeholder*: the composite primitive avatars (spheres/cylinders/cubes, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:339-380`), the fountain built from cylinders (82-115), the viewmodel weapon cubes (384-423), the fallback tinted boxes (240-249), the fallback marker cylinders (259-262), and the billboarded 128px face-bubble emotes (`FaceTexture.cpp`). Several of these carry "legacy"/"placeholder"/"v1" comments (e.g. `RaylibRenderer.cpp:241, 260, 299`, `RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).

**(2) Actual color/lighting mood.** Warm, low-poly, low-saturation daytime: light-blue sky `135,190,235`, warm-desaturated grass `116,153,86`, grey-brown asphalt/sidewalk/plaza. Lighting is not directional — it is one global brightness scalar (1.0 day → 0.35 night, `DayNight.hpp:56`) multiplied per-fragment, plus a fixed warm tint `1.06,1.0,0.92` (`Assets.cpp:61`). Dusk pushes a strong orange `222,136,84`; night is a deep navy `16,22,44`. Everything melts into the sky color via exp² distance fog. Net mood: hazy, warm, flat-lit stylized daytime town — no shadows, no specular, no highlights.

**(3) Coherence of KayKit models + primitive composites + shader fog.** The fog shader is the unifying layer — it is bound to every model material AND wraps the primitive batch, so models and primitives haze/brighten identically (`Assets.cpp:226-230, 265-269`; `RaylibRenderer.cpp:154-160`). That gives atmospheric coherence. Form-language coherence is weaker: textured KayKit low-poly models sit next to untextured flat-shaded primitive avatars, a primitive fountain, and cube weapons — different construction idioms unified only by palette warmth and the shared fog/brightness pass.

**(4) Texture/material work vs flat-shaded solids.** Split. The KayKit models carry their own textures/materials (e.g. `citybits_texture.png`, `Assets.cpp:101`) sampled by the shader's `texture0 * colDiffuse * fragColor` (`Assets.cpp:60`). Everything drawn by the renderer itself is flat-shaded solid color with no texture and no normal-based shading: ground/road/slab constants (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:20-24`), fountain stone/water (87-89), composite-avatar palette colors (327-330), viewmodel colors (394-396), fallback tints (242-247). The only procedural texture is the baked face emote (`FaceTexture.cpp`). No normal maps, no PBR, no per-pixel lighting anywhere.

**Note:** `RaylibRenderer.hpp:3-5` still carries a "NOT YET IN THE BUILD" header comment referencing plan steps 1-3, though the .cpp is fully implemented — worth verifying against `CMakeLists.txt` if you cite build status.
